name: a_movers_session
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Session movers.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
US stocks >= $2B market cap making the biggest moves in the regular session (CNBC / MarketWatch / Barron's / Investopedia / Reuters mover roundups): % move and the stated catalyst for each.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **CRWV** — AI Infrastructure
- CoreWeave shares closed about 6% higher on Thursday after reversing earlier losses; CNBC attributed the prior selling pressure to concerns that the company and other AI infrastructure firms were borrowing heavily to fund expansion. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[1]
- CoreWeave had earlier traded down about 2% in CNBC’s midday roundup before reversing higher by the close. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[1]

## **RKLB** — Space / Communications & Networking
- Rocket Lab fell about 11% after delaying the launch of its Neutron rocket to 2027. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[1]

## **PAG** — Automotive / Industrials
- Penske Automotive rose 8% after announcing it would be taken private by Motown Acquisition Corp., owned by Penske Corp. and Mitsui, for $212 per share in cash. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[1]

## **WMT** — Retail
- Walmart rose more than 2% after Deutsche Bank upgraded the shares from hold to buy and raised its price target from $113 to $136, citing a positive outlook for 2027. (Investopedia, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[4]

## **CROX** — Retail
- Crocs gained 6% after Barclays upgraded the shares from equal weight to overweight. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[1]

## **KMB** — Retail / Consumer Staples
- Kimberly-Clark gained about 4% after issuing preliminary third-quarter results that exceeded Wall Street estimates. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[1]

## **MRSH** — Financials
- Marsh & McLennan rose 5% after reporting third-quarter revenue and earnings above Wall Street estimates. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[1]

## **NKE** — Retail
- Nike rose about 6% on Thursday and led Dow gainers; Investopedia reported that the stock had been down 45% for the year before the session. (Investopedia, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[4]

## **IP** — Specialty Materials
- International Paper rose 7% after saying it was evaluating unsolicited inbound inquiries regarding its EMEA Packaging Business and was in discussions with potential bidders. (Investopedia, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[4]

## **CRM** — Software & SaaS
- Salesforce gained almost 4% as software stocks rose while the broader technology sector declined. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[1]

## **ADBE** — Software & SaaS
- Adobe rose more than 3% during Thursday’s session as software stocks outperformed declining chipmakers. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[1]

## **ORCL** — Software & SaaS
- Oracle climbed 2% during Thursday’s session as the software sector gained. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[1]

## **NVDA / AMD / MRVL** — Semiconductors
- Nvidia fell nearly 2%, while Advanced Micro Devices and Marvell Technology each fell more than 3% as chipmakers declined; the VanEck Semiconductor ETF was down about 2% and headed for an eighth consecutive losing session. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[1]

## **ANET / LRCX / GEV / KLAC** — Semiconductors / AI Infrastructure
- Arista Networks fell 8.43%, Lam Research 7.22%, GE Vernova 4.85%, and KLA 4.92% in Thursday trading; the cited roundup did not provide individual catalysts. (Investing.com, Oct 15, 10:36 ET)[7]

## **MAN / AEHR / PENG / VIAV / FORM / AXTI** — Industrials / Semiconductors
- Manpower fell 15.69%, Aehr Test Systems 10.65%, Smart Global Holdings 10.36%, JDS Uniphase 9.60%, FormFactor 9.62%, and AXT 9.82% in Thursday trading; the cited roundup did not provide individual catalysts. (Investing.com, Oct 15, 10:36 ET)[7]

## Macro / Markets
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1.08% to 52,177.69, the S&P 500 rose 0.33% to 7,744.06, and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.08% to 26,713.03 on Thursday. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[8]
- The session included a rotation away from technology stocks; consumer staples advanced, with Campbell’s up about 5% and General Mills and Conagra Brands each up more than 3%. (CNBC, Oct 15, publication time not stated)[1]
